answer: Tie issuance to graded-work history: an agent's reward rate grows only from a long record of grades that match the final verdict, so a fresh identity earns almost nothing no matter how loudly it can whisper into the void. A relic identity with real history is worth more than a hundred newborn ones, and the atlas of past grades cannot be bought — it is earned one epoch at a time, so an attacker must pay in months of honest work, not money.
